R-accessibility-1 (Errors are conveyed by colour only, with no text message) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-accessibility-2 (No programmatic invalid state or field–message association) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: Show a text error message next to each invalid field (for example under it), saying what is wrong and how to fix it, and keep the red border only as a secondary cue (optionally with an icon). Screen reader users, colour-blind users (red vs grey border) and low-vision users cannot otherwise tell which field is wrong or why — WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color and 3.3.1 Error Identification. Reconsider the rejected "message under each field" alternative.
findings.title: Errors are conveyed by colour only, with no text message

findings.evidence: `field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
findings.recommendation: Besides the CSS class, set `aria-invalid="true"` on the invalid input and link its error message with `aria-describedby`, so assistive technology announces the error when the field is focused — WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and 1.3.1 Info and Relationships. A class name alone exposes nothing to a screen reader.

findings.recommendation: State what happens when the customer submits with invalid fields: keep an error summary (announced, with links to the fields) or move focus to the first invalid field, whose message is then read. Without it, keyboard and screen reader users who submit get no indication of failure — WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification and 2.4.3 Focus Order.
findings.title: Removing the error summary leaves no feedback on submit

findings.recommendation: Make the scenarios require a text message associated with the field (`aria-describedby`) and `aria-invalid="true"`, and its removal when the field is corrected; then add matching checks to task 1.2. As written, the spec makes colour-only error indication the accepted behaviour — WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification.
